listings.name: Hightower Business Park
listings.headline: Hightower Business Park | Premier Class A Industrial Development | Up to 1.8M SF
listings.description:
Hightower is a premier Class A industrial development strategically located at 6000 McHard Road in Houston’s thriving Fort Bend County with a proposed six building offering totaling 1.8 million square feet, this master-planned park is engineered for operational excellence and scalable logistics. Each building features whitebox warehouse interiors, ESFR sprinkler systems, and oversized ramps, with clear heights ranging from 32’ to 36’ to accommodate diverse tenant needs.

The site offers secure truck courts, abundant trailer storage, and high-volume dock high doors with multiple dock levelers rated at 40,000 lbs. Speculative office suites are available starting at 50,000 SF, with custom layouts and two-story configurations in select buildings. Tenants benefit from LED lighting, HVLS warehouse fans, and robust power infrastructure including transformers up to 3,000 kVA.
Positioned near major thoroughfares including FM 521, Sam Houston Tollway, and Highway 288, Hightower ensures seamless access to Houston’s core districts, the Texas Medical Center, and key distribution routes. Drive times to Houston CBD, I-10, and HOU Airport are under 30 minutes, with extended reach to Austin, San Antonio, and Dallas within 3–4 hours.

Fort Bend County’s Triple Freeport Tax Exemption and pro-business climate further enhance the value proposition for logistics, manufacturing, and distribution tenants. With over 500,000 higher education students and a nationally ranked workforce, Hightower is primed to support long-term growth and operational success.

listings.headline: Historic Route 66 Commercial Building for Sale
listings.description:
Executive Summary

Own a piece of the “Mother Road” with this exceptional commercial opportunity at 3314 E. 11th Street, situated in the heart of Tulsa—the officially designated Capital of Route 66. 

Originally constructed in 1930 and occupied by Safeway as early as 1951, this building is a rare surviving example of the mid-sized commercial architecture that defined 11th Street’s storied history during the golden age of American travel. 

Today, the property benefits from its location in the heart of a vibrant, high-traffic corridor that draws both international tourism and consistent local commerce. The building’s historic pedigree, combined with its prominent frontage on 11th Street / HWY 66, provides an exceptional foundation for a variety of adaptive reuse or investment ventures.

listings.name: Pep Boys
listings.headline: CORPORATE GUARANTEE | 2% ANNUAL INCREASES
listings.description:
CBRE is pleased to offer to the market this Pep Boys property with approximately 10 years left on the lease. The lease is corporate backed, absolute net and carries 2% annual rent escalations throughout the remainder of the initial term.  The tenant has four, 5 year options to extend their term at fair market value.  The property was built in 2008 as a Just Brakes location and was remodeled in 2017 after Pep Boys purchased the Just Brakes franchise.  The property is well positioned down the street from HEB’s Distribution Center, Manufacturing Plant and Retail Support Center; positioned across the street from Ross Dress for Less and HEB ahcnored shopping centers and minutes to Fort Sam Houston Airforce Base with a population of 160,000 People and San Antonio Military Medical Center, the larest military medical training facility in the world. 

Pep Boys is an American automotive aftermarket service chain. Originally named Pep Auto Supply, the company was founded in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1921 by Emanuel "Manny" Rosenfeld, Maurice "Moe" Strauss, W. Graham "Jack" Jackson, and Moe Radavitz. Pep Boys is headquartered in the Philadelphia suburb of Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania. The company provides name-brand tires, automotive maintenance and repair, and fleet maintenance and repair to customers across the United States. As of 2016, the company operated more than 9,000 service bays in 35 states and Puerto Rico and the Pep Boys Mobile Crew service trailer, which offers automotive maintenance on location.
listings.locationDescription:
With over 300 years of history, as the only UNESCO World Heritage Site in Texas and one of only two Creative Cities of Gastronomy in the entire United States, there is so much to appreciate in San Antonio. San Antonio is the county seat of Bexar County, Texas. The city is the seventh most populous in the US, the second largest in the Southern US, and the second most populous in Texas.  Straddling the regional divide between South and Central Texas, San Antonio anchors the southwestern corner of an urban megaregion colloquially known as the Texas Triangle. Downtown San Antonio and Downtown Austin are approximately 80 miles apart, both falling along the Interstate 35 corridor. Some observers expect the two metropolitan regions to form a new metroplex similar to Dallas and Fort Worth. 

San Antonio has a diversified economy with a gross domestic product of more than $144 billion in 2021. According to the San Antonio Convention and Visitors Bureau, the city is visited by about 37 million tourists a year, contributing substantially to its economy, primarily due to The Alamo and the River Walk. Tourism provides over 130,000 jobs, and has an economic impact of $15.2 billion in the local economy. The city of San Antonio receives approximately $195 million a year from the hospitality industry, with revenues from hotel occupancy tax, sales taxes and others. The Henry B. Gonzalez Convention Center alone hosts over 300 events annually with more than 750,000 convention delegates from around the world. 

San Antonio is the headquarters of four Fortune 500 companies as well as 15+ smaller companies including: Valero Energy, USAA, iHeartMedia, and NuStar Energy. H-E-B, the 13th-largest private company in the U.S., is also headquartered in San Antonio. The North American Development Bank, a development finance institution jointly held by the governments of the U.S. and Mexico, is headquartered in San Antonio as well. In December 2020, Amazon announced plans to for three new facilities in San Antonio and the city is home to the South Texas Medical Center, the only medical research and care provider in the South Texas region.

San Antonio boasts one of the largest concentrations of military bases in the U.S., and has been nicknamed "Military City, USA".  They are home to U.S. Air Force Basic Military Training (AFBMT). The Air Force only has one location for enlisted basic training: the 737th Training Group, at Lackland Air Force Base. All new Air Force recruits go through the same basic training at Lackland. Each year, over 35,000 new recruits go through AFBMT. In addition, METC (the Military Education and Training Campus), which provides the medical training for the U.S. military at Fort Sam Houston, hosts 30 programs and over 24,000 annual graduates. It is the largest medical education center in the world. The city hosts over 100,000 students in its 31 higher-education institutions. Publicly supported schools include UT Health San Antonio, the University of Texas at San Antonio, Texas A&M University–San Antonio, and the Alamo Community College District. The University of Texas at San Antonio is San Antonio's largest university.

The subject property sits along the neighborhood boundaries of East Side and Alamo Heights.  From St. Paul Square, a bustling dining and entertainment district, to Dignowity Hill, a vintage residential suburb undergoing tremendous revitalization, diversity drives the attraction of San Antonio’s East Side. The East Side of San Antonio is home to the San Antonio Stock Show & Rodeo, the AT&T Center, and the Freeman Coliseum. Adjacent to the Broadway Cultural Corridor, the Alamo Heights neighborhood is centrally located, easily accessible and bursting with entertainment for visitors of all ages. Today, that neighborhood is a city surrounded by San Antonio and filled with locally-owned restaurants, boutiques, museums and parks. All just a few miles north of downtown.

listings.name: La Bajada
listings.headline: 6,421 Acres Located along Interstate 25 between Albuquerque and Santa Fe, NM
listings.description:
CBRE LAND SERVICES GROUP has been engaged as the exclusive listing
representative for the sale of La Bajada. The property consists of approximately
±6,421 acres of vacant land of which includes ±5,200 acres of rich aggregate
deposits for possible mining. (See Buildolgy correspondence).

La Bajada is the largest privately owned parcel of land located on Interstate
25 between Albuquerque and Santa Fe in New Mexico. It features over 10,000
feet of Interstate 25 frontage with two major north and south interchanges
into the site. Exit 264 (State Highway 16) located at the northwest corner of
the property connects to the Cochiti Indian Reservation and Santo Domingo
Pueblo. Exit 267 (County Road 57) is at the northeast corner of the La Bajada
property and connects Highway 14 to the Madrid/Cerrillos Mountains. La Bajada
is approximately 35 minutes from the Albuquerque International Sunport and 15
minutes from Santa Fe Plaza.

This exceptional property has tremendous development potential, both in
terms of a residential master plan and as an aggregate resource. La Bajada is
uniquely situated between Albuquerque, New Mexico’s largest metro area with a
population of over 912,115, and the exclusive Santa Fe market. With an elevation
of over 6,100 feet, La Bajada’s terrain is rich and has varied scenic views from
within the heart of the property, including views of Santa Fe National Forest,
Cerrillos Mountains, Jemez Mountains, Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Sandia
Mountains and the Ortiz Mountains.

The general area is recognized for its mining and railroad history. Existing mines
within the area include Rosario and older mining towns of Waldo, Cerrillos and
Madrid all adding to the ambiance of the area. Even today, the main rail line to
northern New Mexico and Colorado runs through the heart of the land with a
Rail Runner spur coming directly off the main line within the site. The light rail
commuter train carries travelers from Albuquerque through to Santa Fe.

listings.name: The Wiley Building
listings.headline: Class A Medical / Professional Office for Sale or Lease
listings.description: Originally constructed around 1910, the Wiley Building at 1125 Texas began as a four-story industrial concrete warehouse with a basement. Built during El Paso’s early 20th-century industrial expansion, the structure’s heavy concrete design was typical of the era and served as a warehouse and industrial facility, supporting distribution and industrial activity in the rapidly growing downtown area. In the 2010s and early 2020s, the building underwent a complete architectural transformation led by Wright & Dalbin Architects, evolving into a Class A contemporary office structure while preserving its original industrial character. Today, the Wiley Building functions as a mixed medical and professional office building, housing notable tenants such as Salt + Honey Bakery Café, the Advanced Surgery Center of El Paso, the El Paso Orthopedic and Spine Institute, Epiphany Dermatology, El Paso Head and Neck Surgery, and Moreno Cardenas Inc. This modernization, along with ongoing tenant-specific renovations including medical office build-outs and a new ambulatory surgery center on the 5th floor, has positioned the building as a key component in the revitalization of downtown El Paso. The Wiley Building’s adaptive reuse, which preserves historical aspects while incorporating modern elements, makes it one of downtown El Paso’s most noteworthy projects.

highlights: Ground-floor retail including popular on-site dining

listings.headline: 10.9 Acres with Residential Development Potential
listings.description:
CBRE is pleased to present an opportunity to purchase 10.9 acres of land in Logan, Utah.  This property has 6.6 water shares of irrigation with Blacksmith Fork Irrigation and 12 water shares with Spring Creek Irrigation.

This property currently resides in Cache County on the border of Logan’s city boundary, with A-10 zoning which allows for 1 unit per 10 acres. The property is eligible for immediate annexation into Logan City, and has the potential for residential development. Surrounding development has been designated as DR - Detached Residential zoning. DR zoning allows for detached single-family structures with a density of 4-6 dwelling units per acre, with a variety of lot and home sizes to create stable, diverse neighborhoods.
listings.locationDescription: Located on 1800 South, near Hwy 89/91, the main artery into Logan.

listings.headline: 139 Acres for Sale at Newton Reservoir
listings.description: CBRE is pleased to present an opportunity to purchase land located at Newton Reservoir. This property is fronted on two sides by major roads, State Highway 142 on the North and 5800 West on the East and Newton Dam on the South and West. It has a nice general slope with spectacular views overlooking Newton Dam Reservoir and the Clarkston Valley. The property can be subdivided into 10 acre lots each, many with frontage on one of the two main roads. The property comes with irrigation rights out of Newton Dam with an irrigation main line that runs through the property. The property is being rented by a local farmer who has raised wheat, safflower and hay over the years. Additionally, there is a shop building with a front overhead door, with wood frame construction inside, and metal siding outside. This property has great recreational development potential or would be an amazing estate lot, with private access to Newton Reservoir.
listings.locationDescription: Located at Newton Reservoir, and just 20 minutes to Logan, Utah.

listings.locationDescription:
The property is well situated just off of Interstate 84, an east/west interstate connecting Oregon, Idaho and Utah (770 miles).  Given the property's location directly off of the interstate and given Mountain Home's location between the major markets of Boise (40 miles northwest) and Twin Falls (85 miles southeast), as well as their extremely close proximity to the proposed Shoshone-Bannock Casino site, the property is well positioned to take advantage of sales not only from their population of more than 16,000 but also the commuters and tourists looking for equitable snacks and groceries on their travels.  The property is surrounded by many national retail brands, is located just 15 miles from the Mountain Home Air Force Base and is the only discount grocer for 50 miles in any direction.  As such, this tenant is well positioned for long-term stability and growth in this location.


Mountain Home is the largest city, and county seat, of Elmore County, Idaho. As of 2022, the city’s population was 16,469. Mountain Home is the principal city of the Mountain Home Micropolitan Statistical Area, which includes Elmore County. Mountain Home Air Force Base, housing 3,184 residents, is an Air Combat Command installation location 12 miles southwest of the city. Opened in 1943 during World War II, it was originally a bomber training base and later an operational Strategic Air Command bomber and missile base (1953-65). It switched to Tactical Air Command and fighters in January 1966, which was succeeded by Air Combat Command in 1992. 


Tourism has played an important role in Mountain Home’s growth. Visitors and residents alike enjoy a wide variety of local recreational activities offered by Mountain Home’s surroundings. Their city has a strong sense of family values and community that you can experience firsthand at their many local events. Mountain Home is also a haven for outdoor lovers visiting the sand dunes, hiking along mountain-side back trails, casting a line at one of their many fishing destinations, or setting up camp and enjoying the remarkable scenic views.


New local entrepreneurs are opening businesses, established businesses are expanding and outside businesses are looking their way! The City of Mountain Home is taking full advantage of all these positive changes by making changes of their own to improve its community.

listings.name: The Villas Portfolio
listings.headline: THE VILLAS PORTFOLIO, FEATURING ASSUMABLE 2.99% FULL-TERM I/O LOANS ON 222-UNITS IN THE LAS VEGAS VALLEY
listings.description:
The CBRE Las Vegas Multifamily Group presents the opportunity to acquire The Villas Portfolio, comprised of two value-add, garden-style multifamily communities in Las Vegas: Reno Villas and El Parque Villas. Totaling 222 units, The Villas Portfolio offers investors strong in-place cash flow with additional interior and exterior value-add opportunities, with the rare benefit of highly accretive assumable financing.

Located in Southeast Las Vegas, Reno Villas is a 122-unit community built in 1980. The property offers a mix of one-bedroom/one-bathroom and two-bedroom/two-bathroom floor plans, averaging 659 square feet. Residents of Reno Villas enjoy mature landscaping throughout the property, a swimming pool and spa, a fitness center, and laundry facilities. Reno Villas is strategically situated near major employment hubs including, the Las Vegas Strip (+/-400,000 jobs), the future Las Vegas A’s ballpark (16,000 construction jobs; 5,400 permanent jobs), the future Hard Rock Las Vegas Resort (2,500 construction jobs; 6,000 permanent jobs), UNLV, and Harry Reid International Airport. 

El Parque Villas is a 100-unit, garden-style community located in the Southwest submarket of Las Vegas. The property consists of nine, two-story buildings offering one-bedroom/one-bath, and two-bedroom/two-bath units averaging 808 square feet, with 23 units containing private backyards. This asset is ideally positioned near the Las Vegas Medical District (16,000+ projected jobs by 2030), UNLV School of Medicine Campus, Chinatown (1.8 million total SF of retail), The Las Vegas Strip (+/-400,000 jobs), and Downtown Las Vegas (Nine major resorts/casinos), providing residents with convenient access to key employment centers and urban amenities. 

The assets within The Villas Portfolio can be acquired either individually or as a portfolio, and can be acquired unencumbered or as loan assumption acquisition to capitalize on the highly accretive in-place debt at each property. To explore financing options and schedule a tour, please contact our team. You can reach out to Adam Schmitt at +1 702 767 3623, Jannie Mongkolsakulkit at +1 702 369 4801, or Justin Neubeck at +1 702 885 4186​​​​​​​.

listings.locationDescription:
The Greater Yakima metro area is situated east-west in a landscape of gentle slopes and rich silt-loamy soils of a river basin. Looking north you see Yakima Ridge-Cleman Mountain with Mount Rainier in the background, and the Naches River flowing through the valley. As you look south you see Rattlesnake Hills-Ahtanum Ridge with Mount Adams in the background. The Yakima River flows north-south through the Selah and Union Gaps connecting the Kittitas Valley with the greater Yakima Valley.

The Yakima Valley is surrounded by numerous recreation areas - Mount Rainier National Park, the Mount Adams, Goat Rocks and William O. Douglas wilderness areas; the Wenatchee National Forest; Yakima Scenic River; many lakes and streams; the Oak Creek, L.T. Murray, and Saddle Mountain wildlife areas; and the Hanford Reach National Monument. Other recreation areas include the Ahtanum Multiple Use Area; Toppenish National Wildlife Refuge; White Pass Scenic Byway; Mather Memorial Parkway; and Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail.

The Yakima metro area and surrounding yakima valley hosts an arid semi-dry climate conducive to dry summers and cool winters with light snow fall. This makes Yakima a mild area to live and plays into it‘s steadily increasing population in the last decade and the years to come.

The south-central Washington city of Yakima is a growing area with a plethora of amenities and opportunities.

listings.name: Super 8 & Suites by Wyndham
listings.headline: Super 8 & Suites by Wyndham | Indio, CA | Closest Hotel to Empire Polo Grounds
listings.description:
CBRE is proud to present the sale of the Super 8 & Suites by Wyndham Indio, a 92-room, economy-scale hospitality asset located at 81753 CA-111 in the high-growth, festival-driven market of Indio, California. 

This offering represents a compelling opportunity for private investors, hospitality groups, and institutional stakeholders to acquire a stabilized asset in the "City of Festivals. Situated on 1.87 acres with a 21,430 square-foot building, the property benefits from a prime location on Highway 111, offering excellent connectivity to the Interstate 10 corridor and the primary entertainment venues of the Coachella Valley.

Offered at $9,750,000 ($105,978 per key), this property presents huge operational upside with a 9.35% current yield and a 16.94% Pro Forma capitalization rate based on previous owner records. The asset is currently self-managed; however, a new, experienced owner can significantly increase income and optimize operations to reach historical performance levels based on a projected Net Operating Income of $1,651,380. This represents a rare lucrative entry point into the valley’s most populous and internationally recognized tourism and high-volume festival markets.

Built in 1988, the economy class property features 92 well-appointed rooms, a product ideally suited for the region’s high-volume seasonal demand. Guest amenities enhance the appeal, including an outdoor pool, breakfast area, BBQ pit, on-site guest laundry facility,  and 104 surface parking spaces, all contributing to a reliable experience for festival-goers and transient travelers alike. 

The hotel has undergone significant capital investment, including a comprehensive 2012 renovation and ongoing brand maintenance, ensuring a competitive, refreshed product that is fully aligned with Wyndham’s latest standards. This turn-key condition allows for immediate stabilized performance and maximizes immediate cash flow potential.

The investment is underpinned by Indio's recognition as a vibrant community for arts and entertainment, education, commerce, and culture. The local economy benefits from a massive contribution in spending from the hospitality sector, specifically budget hotel tourism, which accounts for millions in annual revenue. Indio is home to more than 20 hotels that, along with robust short-term rentals and music festival campers, generate $4 million to $5 million per year in Transient Occupancy Tax. Furthermore, the city welcomes short-term vacation rentals, which contribute $68 million in spending locally. Festival-goers are eager for rentals as well as luxury, boutique, and budget hotels located in such close proximity to the event grounds.

Furthermore, the hotel is strategically positioned to capitalize on these powerful demand drivers, located only 3 miles from the Empire Polo Club—home to the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival and Stagecoach Country Music Festival. This proximity ensures the property remains a primary choice for a wide demographic of the 2.4 million unique annual visitors to the city. Its location near JFK Memorial Hospital and the expanding College of the Desert Indio Campus further ensures steady year-round commercial demand, presenting immense ENTERPRISE POTENTIAL for the next owner.

This is a unique opportunity to acquire a premium hospitality property in a dynamic desert hub within Riverside County. This asset represents a valuable long-term investment, perfectly suited for institutional professionals looking to expand their portfolio or those engaged in a 1031 Exchange. With its Wyndham brand affiliation, recent turn-key renovations, and location within one of Southern California's most desirable and high-demand markets, the property offers exceptional stability and enduring value for generations.
listings.locationDescription:
Strategic Economic Drivers: The Coachella Valley’s Largest Hub
Indio’s strategic position as the largest and fastest-growing city in the Coachella Valley provides unparalleled regional access across Riverside County via the Interstate 10 corridor. As the primary gateway to the east valley, the city serves as a critical link between the Southern California coast and the greater Inland Empire, solidifying its role as a major regional commerce and hospitality hub. Furthermore, the area is poised for sustained economic uplift as the undisputed "#1" destination for large-scale tourism in the region, driven by its world-famous reputation and its status as the most populous city in the valley. This geographic dominance ensures a steady flow of regional traffic and high-capacity demand for modern accommodations.


Global Festival Impact and Year-Round Tourism
Known worldwide as the "City of Festivals," Indio’s economy is anchored by its status as a global entertainment powerhouse. The city hosts the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival and the Stagecoach Country Music Festival, which together generate a massive global economic impact and attract hundreds of thousands of high-spending visitors annually. This international draw guarantees an influx of high-ADR demand from spectators, production staff, media, and corporate sponsors throughout the peak festival season. Beyond these marquee events, the city’s demographics reflect a rapidly expanding permanent population, providing a resilient base of local demand that complements the massive surge in international tourism and seasonal festival-driven revenue.


Local Demand Generators: Retail, Recreation, and Polo Grounds
Indio’s local economy is bolstered by high-volume retail centers and premier recreational attractions. The city is home to the Empire Polo Club and Eldorado Polo Club, world-renowned venues that serve as the epicenter for both professional polo and the aforementioned global festivals. This leisure draw is complemented by a robust selection of shopping sites and regional power centers that capture significant retail trade activity from across the Coachella Valley. The property further benefits from Indio’s extensive "recreation and entertainment" infrastructure, including championship golf courses and proximity to the Joshua Tree National Park entrance, which attracts millions of outdoor enthusiasts annually. This powerful combination of festival fame, desert recreation, and retail appeal ensures deep, year-round market demand.
highlights: HIGH-YIELD GENERATIONAL WEALTH ACQUISITION: A rare opportunity to acquire a stabilized, 92-room Wyndham-branded asset in the high-growth Indio market. This property offers a low-barrier entry into the Coachella Valley’s resilient tourism sector, making it an ideal vehicle for long-term wealth preservation or a 1031 Exchange.

$9.75M PRICING & HUGE OPERATIONAL UPSIDE: Offered at $9,750,000 ($105,978 per key), this property presents huge operational upside with a 9.35% current yield and a 16.94% Pro Forma capitalization rate based on previous owner records. The asset is currently self-managed; however, a new, experienced owner can significantly increase income and optimize operations to reach historical performance levels based on a projected Net Operating Income of $1,651,380.

listings.locationDescription:
Riverside County, California, is the fourth largest county in California and the tenth largest in the United States. It covers more than 7,300 square miles and is home to 2.4 million residents. Riverside County was created in 1893 from parts of San Diego and San Bernardino counties. The county’s name comes from the City of Riverside, which was named in 1871. To the east lies the vibrant Coachella Valley, home to Desert Hot Springs, a city renowned as a world-class wellness destination and the "spa city" of the desert.

Desert Hot Springs spans 30 square miles and serves as a strategic gateway between the Coachella Valley and the high desert leading to Joshua Tree National Park. Known for its "Healing Oasis," it features a unique collection of boutique spa resorts sitting atop a world-famous natural mineral water aquifer. Together, these regions form a hub of activity across Riverside County, located roughly 100 miles east of downtown Los Angeles. While Riverside is celebrated as the "City of Arts and Innovation," Desert Hot Springs is gaining recognition for its rapid growth, housing 34,000 residents and offering natural landmarks like the Mission Creek Preserve and Cabot’s Pueblo Museum.


The Inland Empire and Coachella Valley feature a network of innovation centers that drive investment and job growth. Riverside has experienced $1.5 billion in private investment in the past five years, while Desert Hot Springs has become a primary engine for the region's hospitality and renewable energy expansion. As a key player in the Coachella Valley’s $9 billion tourism economy, Desert Hot Springs has attracted significant investment in specialized wellness resorts and green energy initiatives, cementing its status as a vital health and sustainability hub.

Both cities offer a more affordable alternative to major coastal hubs like Los Angeles. In Desert Hot Springs, the local economy is buoyed by a flourishing health-and-wellness sector, with city initiatives focused on small business incentives and infrastructure. To support this growth, the region is benefiting from major infrastructure improvements across Riverside County, including the expansion of the Palm Springs International Airport to enhance global connectivity. This collaborative economic environment across the Riverside-Coachella Valley corridor makes the region a premier choice for entrepreneurs and businesses looking for a resilient, business-friendly climate in Southern California.

Recreation & entertainment
Anchored by two historic performing arts centers, downtown Riverside offers the best in nightlife and entertainment, including the famed Festival of Lights. Complementing Riverside’s urban cultural scene, Desert Hot Springs offers premier wellness and outdoor recreation. It is home to some of the purest natural hot and cold mineral springs in the world and provides extensive hiking trails that showcase the Coachella Valley’s rugged beauty. Between Riverside’s lively restaurant scene and the tranquil "spa city" appeal of Desert Hot Springs, the area offers a diverse quality of life that caters to both urban energy and restorative desert tranquility.

The City of Palm Springs, incorporated in 1938 on the ancestral lands of the Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians, stands as a historical cornerstone known for its world-class mid-century modern architecture. As a global hub for luxury tourism located 100 miles east of Los Angeles, it offers a rich cultural tapestry fueled by international festivals and a vibrant arts community.

The City of Palm Springs is committed to building strategic partnerships for sustainable economic development through initiatives that stimulate a favorable investment climate, welcome entrepreneurship, and support industry diversity. As a premier destination for innovation and wellness, Palm Springs is the city of choice in the desert: a place where diverse talents choose to work and where businesses choose to invest. The City offers a legendary brand, a stable real estate market, and a business-friendly environment that is unique to the Southern California desert.

A lively culinary scene featuring world-renowned international cuisine is a constant in the city, with numerous annual events, including the signature Coachella and Stagecoach festivals (highlighting the region’s massive “festival economy”), the Palm Springs International Film Festival, and Modernism Week regularly enlivening the desert core. San Bernardino County is the largest county in the contiguous United States, encompassing over 20,000 square miles. Its vast and diverse geography ranges from the high-density urban valleys of the Inland Empire to the expansive, sparsely populated Mojave Desert and the scenic San Bernardino Mountains. The county seat is the city of San Bernardino, which is the most populous city and a major hub for both government and transportation. The county's history is rich with influences from Native American tribes, Spanish missionaries, and Mormon pioneers, all of which are reflected in its many historic landmarks.


The county's economic landscape is driven by its strategic location and diverse industries. As a major logistics and transportation hub, it features numerous large-scale warehouse and distribution centers. Key economic drivers also include professional business services, healthcare, and tourism, particularly in mountain resorts like Big Bear and Lake Arrowhead. San Bernardino County’s economy benefits from its affordability compared to coastal California cities and a workforce supported by institutions like Crafton Hills College, making it an attractive environment for new businesses and residents seeking opportunities in a growing region.


Yucaipa is a city within the larger Inland Empire region of Southern California, which includes both San Bernardino and Riverside counties. The city's economic strategy is to balance its small-town, rural character with new opportunities for business and growth. The City of Yucaipa is actively working to attract diverse industries, including biotech manufacturing, medical supplies, and food processing, leveraging its affordable land costs and available workforce. As part of the broader Inland Empire, Yucaipa's economic development is intertwined with the region's strong logistics and transportation sectors, and the city is strategically focusing on its Freeway Corridor to facilitate commercial and industrial expansion. The Yucaipa Chamber of Commerce and city officials are collaborating to foster a business-friendly environment that encourages entrepreneurship and supports a wide range of industries, all while aiming to maintain the high quality of life that defines the community.


Yucaipa and the greater San Bernardino County offer a wide range of recreational and entertainment opportunities, moving beyond the nightlife and festivals of larger cities. Yucaipa itself is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, with Yucaipa Regional Park providing amenities like fishing lakes, swimming, camping, and hiking trails that take advantage of the city's scenic location in the foothills of the San Bernardino Mountains. The city also boasts the Yucaipa Performing Arts Center (YPAC), a modern venue that hosts a variety of concerts, theatrical productions, and community events. Annual festivals like the Yucaipa Music & Arts Festival and the Yucaipa Rodeo celebrate the city's culture and heritage, drawing residents and visitors alike.


Beyond Yucaipa, San Bernardino County is home to a host of significant entertainment venues. The Glen Helen Amphitheater, managed by Live Nation, is a massive outdoor concert venue that attracts major national and international touring acts. The county's vast size also provides opportunities for recreation in the nearby mountains, offering skiing, snowboarding, and hiking, as well as desert landscapes for off-roading and other outdoor activities. This diverse blend of local community events, major concert venues, and accessible natural wonders ensures a wide variety of recreational and entertainment options for residents and visitors of Yucaipa and San Bernardino County.

Apple Valley, California, is a premier desert community nestled in the Victor Valley region of San Bernardino County. Situated at the base of the San Bernardino Mountains and just east of the high-growth city of Victorville, Apple Valley offers a unique blend of high-desert beauty and strategic regional connectivity. The property at 19087 Allegheny Road is perfectly positioned within the heart of the 92307 ZIP code, sitting just one block off Highway 18. This primary arterial provides immediate access to the 15 Freeway, the main thoroughfare connecting Southern California to Las Vegas—located approximately 188 miles to the northeast. The area is characterized by its wide-open spaces, scenic mountain views, and a climate that offers a distinct four-season experience within a desert landscape.


The economy of Apple Valley and the surrounding Victor Valley is anchored by a diverse mix of healthcare, logistics, government, and retail trade. A primary economic driver for the immediate neighborhood is the healthcare sector; Allegheny Arms is located just 1.4 miles from St. Mary Medical Center and is within 8 miles of Victor Valley Global Medical Center. These institutions serve as major local employers and provide a stable base of professional tenants. Education also plays a vital role in the local economy, with Victor Valley College serving as a nearby hub for higher learning and workforce development. The region has seen significant growth in the logistics and distribution sector, fueled by its proximity to major transportation corridors and the presence of major employers like Amazon in nearby Victorville. Retail and service industries continue to thrive at centers like Desert Mountain Plaza and the Mall of Victor Valley, catering to a growing population seeking more affordable housing options relative to the coastal Southern California markets.


Apple Valley offers a high quality of life with a wealth of recreational opportunities that celebrate its natural surroundings. The community is renowned for its extensive park system and proximity to outdoor adventure. Residents at Allegheny Arms enjoy on-site leisure amenities like a community pool and barbecue picnic areas surrounded by manicured rose gardens. Locally, the Apple Valley Center and nearby shopping districts offer a variety of dining and entertainment options within a three-mile radius. For the outdoor enthusiast, the region is a gateway to hiking, off-roading, and equestrian trails. The property’s location on the way to Las Vegas also positions it as a convenient starting point for regional travelers. Furthermore, the area’s recreation is bolstered by its proximity to the high-desert’s unique attractions, providing a blend of suburban convenience and rugged natural beauty that continues to attract residents and investors alike.

As of 2023, Portland’s population was 622,882, making it the 26th-most populous city in the United States, and the second-most populous in the Pacific Northwest, after Seattle. Portland’s location is beneficial for several industries. Relatively low energy cost, accessible resources, north–south and east–west Interstates, international air terminals, large marine shipping facilities, and both west coast intercontinental railroads are all economic advantages. The city’s marine terminals alone handle over 13 million tons of cargo per year, and the port is home to one of the largest commercial dry docks in the country. The Port of Portland is the third-largest export tonnage port on the west coast of the U.S., and being about 80 miles upriver, it is the largest fresh-water port. The scrap steel industry thrives in the region, with Schnitzer Steel Industries, a prominent scrap steel company, ESCO Corporation and Oregon Steel Mills.

Technology is a major component of the city’s economy, with more than 1,200 technology companies existing within the metro. This high density of technology companies has led to the nickname Silicon Forest being used to describe the Portland area, a reference to the abundance of trees in the region and to the Silicon Valley region in Northern California. The area also hosts facilities for software companies and online startup companies, some supported by local seed funding organizations and business incubators. Computer components manufacturer Intel is the Portland area’s largest employer, providing jobs for more than 15,000 people, with several campuses to the west of central Portland in the city of Hillsboro. The Portland metro area has become a business cluster for athletic/outdoor gear and footwear manufacturer’s headquarters. Shoes are not manufactured in Portland. The area is home to the global, North American or U.S. headquarters of Nike, Adidas, Columbia Sportswear, LaCrosse Footwear, Dr. Martens, Li-Ning, Keen, and Hi-Tec Sports. While headquartered elsewhere, Merrell, Amer Sports and Under Armour have design studios and local offices in the Portland area.

Other notable Portland-based companies include industrial goods and metal fabrication company Precision Castparts, film animation studio Laika; commercial vehicle manufacturer Daimler Trucks North America; advertising firm Wieden+Kennedy; bankers Umpqua Holdings; child care and early childhood education provider KinderCare Learning Centers; and retailers Fred Meyer, New Seasons Market, Storables, and Powell’s Books.

Portland, Oregon has over 70 breweries, making it one of the cities in the world with the highest number of breweries. The Portland metropolitan area is also the largest craft brewing market in the United States. Additionally, the city boasts a robust coffee culture that now rivals Seattle and hosts over 20 coffee roasters.

In 2023, visitors to Portland spent $5.4 billion, producing $260 million in state and local tax revenue. The travel industry supports 34,300 jobs in the Portland area, generating $1.7 billion in employment earnings.

listings.locationDescription:
San Bernardino, California, nestled in the heart of the Inland Empire within San Bernardino County, boasts a rich history and a dynamic present. Situated at the base of the San Bernardino Mountains, and just east of the neighboring city of Rialto, San Bernardino has played a crucial role in the region’s development. From its origins as an ancestral Tongva and Serrano settlement to its transformation into a major logistical hub, San Bernardino has witnessed significant growth. The arrival of the Santa Fe Railroad in the late 19th century spurred this expansion, connecting the “Gate City” to the rest of the region and facilitating the transportation of citrus and people. 

Today, San Bernardino is a bustling city with a diverse economy and a vibrant community. It serves as a major transportation hub with easy access to the I-10, I-215, and SR-210 freeways and San Bernardino International Airport, making it a key gateway to the Inland Empire. The city is also home to several popular local landmarks, including the original McDonald’s Site and Museum and the historic California Theatre of the Performing Arts, which draw visitors from all over the region. While precise annual visitor numbers can fluctuate, San Bernardino’s logistical prominence and central location contribute to a significant influx of business and leisure travelers each year. The city’s proximity to the mountains provides residents with opportunities for outdoor recreation, while its rich history is preserved in local architecture and landmarks.

San Bernardino’s economy is a diverse mix of industries, with a strong emphasis on logistics, government, and healthcare. Its strategic location near major transportation corridors has made it a premier hub for massive fulfillment centers, attracting global giants like Amazon, Kohl’s, and Mattel. The city also has a significant manufacturing presence, with companies producing everything from aerospace components to food products and construction materials. Compared to other Inland Empire cities, San Bernardino boasts a robust public sector and industrial base that serves as the “backbone” of the regional economy, contributing heavily to its long-term economic vitality. 

In terms of housing, San Bernardino offers a mix of options, including single-family homes, historic bungalows, and multi-family apartments. While housing costs have risen in recent years, they generally remain more affordable than in neighboring Los Angeles or Orange Counties. This affordability, coupled with the city’s vast job opportunities in the distribution and medical sectors, attracts a diverse range of renters. You’ll find everyone from students and young families to healthcare professionals and industrial workforce members calling San Bernardino home. The city’s ongoing investment in the downtown core and transit-oriented developments suggest that its economy and housing market will continue to thrive.

San Bernardino offers a variety of recreational and entertainment options for residents and visitors alike. The city boasts numerous parks and facilities, such as Seccombe Lake Park and Wildwood Park, providing opportunities for sports, picnicking, and community gatherings. The nearby San Bernardino Mountains offer additional recreational opportunities, including hiking trails, camping, and snow sports just a short drive away. For entertainment, San Bernardino is home to the Glen Helen Amphitheater and the San Manuel Stadium, while the National Orange Show Event Center remains a popular venue for festivals and motorsports enthusiasts. The city also hosts annual community events and seasonal festivals, fostering a sense of local pride and offering entertainment for all ages. While San Bernardino is known for its sprawling residential areas, it offers a selection of local restaurants, craft breweries, and the hospitality of the Hospitality Lane district, ensuring there are plenty of options for shopping and dining out. The proximity to other Inland Empire cities further expands the range of nightlife and cultural entertainment options available within a short drive.

Covering 20,105 square miles, San Bernardino County is America’s largest county and a diverse public service organization governed by an elected Board of Supervisors and serving a community of nearly 2.2 million residents. San Bernardino County is comprised of more than 40 departments and agencies staffed by more than 25,000 public service professionals providing a wide range of vital services in areas that include public safety, health and human services, economic development, housing, recreation, and culture. San Bernardino County offers a variety of job opportunities in fields such as healthcare, public safety, and technology. Given San Bernardino County’s location and relative housing affordability in Southern California, it has become a substantial supplier of housing and construction-related jobs, which are a key employment sectors for the region. 

San Bernardino, nestled against the San Bernardino Mountains and bathed in Californian sunshine, boasts a tapestry of history, cultural diversity, and modern life. Founded in 1810, its heritage echoes in the Mission de San Bernardino and the Santa Fe Depot, remnants of its vibrant past. Today, the city’s heart beats with a mix of urban grit and artistic spirit, evident in its revitalized downtown brimming with restaurants, theaters, and museums. Outdoor enthusiasts find solace in the San Bernardino National Forest, with its hiking trails and breathtaking views. Families create memories at the nostalgic Route 66 Drive-In or the expansive Field Museum of Natural History. Though challenges exist, San Bernardino’s spirit of resilience shines through, evident in its diverse communities and its ongoing pursuit of economic revitalization. This city, bathed in history and embracing change, stands ready to write its next chapter. San Bernardino, CA, stands at an economic crossroads. As the largest city in San Bernardino County, it boasts assets like a strategic location at the crossroads of major transportation arteries and a diverse, young workforce. The city’s economic development department actively pursues business attraction and retention, focusing on key sectors like logistics, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing. use space for businesses and residents. 

The Inland Empire, which includes Riverside and San Bernardino Counties, has a network of innovation centers that drive investment and job growth. San Bernardino County is committed to a thriving city possessing a sustainable system of high-quality education, community health, public safety, housing, retail, recreation, arts and culture and infrastructure. San Bernardino County envisions a world class region which capitalizes on its location, the diversity of its people and its economy to create a broad range of choices for its residents in how they live, work, and play. In addition, it strives for a continual vibrant economy with a skilled workforce that attracts employers who seek the unique opportunities the region has to offer and provide jobs that create area-wide prosperity. 

San Bernardino, California, bursts with annual entertainment options catering to diverse interests. Spring paints the scene with the vibrant Wisteria Festival, boasting colorful blooms, live music, and cultural immersion. Music lovers groove to the energetic beats of Beyond Wonderland and Nocturnal Wonderland, large-scale electronic dance music festivals held under the starry skies. History buffs step back in time at the Route 66 Rendezvous, showcasing classic cars, live entertainment, and nostalgic vibes. Foodies revel in the International Food Festival, a delightful explosion of flavors and aromas from around the globe. And don’t forget the National Orange Show, a citrus extravaganza celebrating the region’s agricultural heritage with amusement rides, exhibits, and citrus-themed fun for all ages. These are just a taste of the annual events that make San Bernardino a hub of entertainment throughout the year.

listings.locationDescription:
Wilsonville is a city primarily in Clackamas County, Oregon. Located within the Portland metropolitan area, the city also includes the planned communities of Charbonneau on the south side of the river, and Villebois, a European-style urban village that earned a national design award, on the western edge. The city is bisected by Interstate 5 and includes I-5’s Boone Bridge over the Willamette.
 
Adjacent Interstate 5, Wilsonville is a business-friendly community that provides an attractive location for manufacturers and distributors. Its location makes it highly 
accessible for commuting employees as well as freight traffic. Connectivity to the 
greater Portland Metro is also advantageous for those seeking proximity to urban 
amenities, a top-rated international airport, the western US coast and the Ports of 
Portland & Seattle. The City’s considerable weekday workforce also supports high 
tech industries, family-owned companies and several local and national retailers. 

Wilsonville has often had more jobs in the city than residents, which has led to the city becoming headquarters for several major local and national companies, as well as home to facilities of several national companies. Companies with their headquarters in the city include design software maker Mentor Graphics; the largest employer in the city, imaging systems manufacturer FLIR Systems; and shoe retailer Solestruck. The city is also home to Stream Global Services, the second largest employer in the city and Xerox, the third largest employer in the city. Wilsonville contains many distribution and manufacturing buildings adjacent to Interstate 5 such as regional distribution facilities for Coca-Cola and Rite Aid. Additionally, available land is creating new opportunities for Wilsonville and business, while city leaders continue working with the regional government Metro and the state of Oregon to plan a 200-acre industrial site in northwest area of the city. The Coffee Creek Industrial area, near the Oregon Coffee Creek Correctional Facility, has been labeled a regionally significant industrial area and is the city’s next area of major business development. The City is in the process now of conducting additional studies and undertaking planning efforts for infrastructure, including roads, sewer and water services. City leaders hope the property lead to 1,500 more family-wage jobs with an annual payroll of $55 million at full build out. Wilsonville’s 1,000-plus businesses provide 20,165 full-time jobs, with over half in high-wage industrial occupations of manufacturing or wholesale distribution. According to the city of Wilsonville, the total annual private-sector payroll in Wilsonville is nearly $1.1 billion annually. That is a 80-percent more than it was in 2000 and generates a total regional economic impact of over $3.2 billion annually.

Wilsonville sits on the north bank of the Willamette River, offering easy access for recreational boaters, canoers and kayakers as well as proximity to the valley’s abundance of award-winning wineries. World-class natural getaways – Mount Hood, the Columbia River Gorge, ocean beaches – all await within a two-hour drive. With its location at the southernmost end of the Portland metropolitan area, Wilsonville is the gateway to the verdant Willamette Valley. Once a small farming community, Wilsonville is now a thriving city of more than 26,000 residents who enjoy the small town feel just 17 miles from Portland. Its southerly location is roughly halfway between the Portland central business district and the state capital in Salem. Wilsonville’s labor force draws from both metro areas.

listings.description:
CBRE, Inc., as exclusive advisor, is pleased to present the opportunity to acquire a stabilized quadruplex located at 412 W Ramona Drive in Rialto, California. 
Located just one block from the historic Route 66 (Foothill Blvd), this one-story property is within walking distance of prime local retail, offering residents an ideal blend of convenience and heritage. This quadruplex presents a rare opportunity to capture a substantial 16% rental upside in the high-demand Inland Empire market, pairing long-term appreciation potential with a stable 5.25% entry cap rate and an 11.27 GRM. With a projected pro forma cap rate of 6.88% upon reaching market rents, the asset is positioned for significant growth. Situated on a generous ±7,686 square foot lot with ±2,760 rentable square feet area, the property provides a low-density living environment that is increasingly sought after in the region.


Strategic Location and Connectivity
Rialto offers a premier family-friendly suburban lifestyle, characterized by a mix of historic charm along Route 66 and expanding modern retail hubs like the Renaissance Marketplace. Strategically positioned near major transportation arteries, the property provides residents with seamless connectivity to Interstates 10, 15, 215, and State Route 210, effectively linking the asset to the broader Inland Empire and Greater Los Angeles employment markets. As a central node in the global supply chain, Rialto supports industry giants such as Amazon and FedEx, driving consistent housing demand. Furthermore, the property’s location offers convenient access to the Kaiser Permanente Medical Center in neighboring Fontana—a major regional employer—alongside an array of essential dining and shopping destinations.


Asset Composition and Property Features
412 W Ramona Drive consists of four identical two-bedroom, one-bathroom floor plans with an average size of 690 square feet. Built in 1961, the residences have been thoughtfully maintained and feature modern interior updates with a mix of carpet and vinyl wood flooring. Each unit is designed for convenience with wall-mounted central air and heating, security doors, and efficient kitchens equipped with gas stoves and oven ranges. The exterior is secured by an iron fence and gate, featuring private porches, private yards, and composition roofs. Residents enjoy dedicated surface parking in the rear of the property in addition to ample street parking. 


Stability and Growth Potential
This offering presents an opportunity to acquire a stabilized, income-producing asset in one of the nation’s most resilient rental markets. Whether for a 1031 exchange buyer or a seasoned investor, 412 W Ramona Drive provides long-term stability and significant growth potential. The combination of current cash flow and the 16% rental upside offers a clear path to value appreciation, underpinned by the strong economic fundamentals and the logistics-driven growth of the Rialto submarket.
listings.locationDescription:
GEOGRAPHIC
Rialto, California, nestled in the western part of the Inland Empire within San Bernardino County, boasts a rich history and a dynamic present. Situated at the foothills of the San Bernardino Mountains, and just east of the neighboring city of Fontana, Rialto has played a crucial role in the region’s development. From its origins as an ancestral Serrano Indian settlement to its transformation into a major industrial hub, Rialto has witnessed significant growth. The arrival of the Santa Fe Railroad in the late 19th century spurred this expansion, connecting the Rialto colony to the rest of the region and facilitating the transportation of citrus and people.


Today, Rialto is a bustling city with a diverse economy and a vibrant community. It serves as a major transportation hub with easy access to the I-10 and I-210 freeways and Ontario International Airport, making it a key gateway to the Inland Empire. The city is also home to several popular local landmarks, including the historic Route 66 corridor and the Rialto Historical Society Museum, which draw visitors from all over the region. While precise annual visitor numbers can fluctuate, Rialto’s logistics prominence and central location contribute to a significant influx of business and leisure travelers each year. The city’s proximity to the mountains provides residents with opportunities for outdoor recreation, while its rich history is preserved in local adobes and landmarks.


GENERAL ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Rialto’s economy is a diverse mix of industries, with a strong emphasis on logistics, manufacturing, and distribution. Its strategic location near major transportation corridors has made it a premier hub for massive fulfillment centers, attracting global giants like Amazon, Target, and FedEx. The city also has a significant manufacturing presence, with companies producing everything from steel and building materials to aerospace components. Compared to other Inland Empire cities, Rialto boasts a robust industrial sector that serves as the “backbone” of the regional supply chain, contributing heavily to its economic vitality.

listings.description:
CBRE is pleased to offer to the market the Willapa Shopping Center, anchored by Thriftway and located in Raymond, WA directly along the Willapa Bay.

The center is well positioned to service several local communities along Highway 101 and Highway 6 as the closest large grocery operators are 25+ miles to the north in Aberdeen, 65+ Miles to the west in Ocean Park, 53 miles south in Astoria, OR and 53 miles to the east in Chehalis. There are more than 10,000 residents and more than 4K households just within a 15-mile radius, not to mention the underserved tenants farther west, south and east, that rely on this Thriftway for their local shopping needs. The Thriftway, on a new 10-year NNN lease, makes up just over 80% of the center. Other tenants like Subway and Las Maracas Mexican restaurant have been long-term tenants of the center at 25+ and 10+ years respectively. The property has excellent visibility from Highway 101, the main north/south highway running up and down the California, Oregon and Washington coasts. The property benefits from out pads housing national tenants McDonald’s and Shell Oil. There are two easily accessible areas of ingress/egress along the sides of the national tenanted out pads and the property itself sits on a large parcel with ample parking at a size of over 4 acres.
listings.locationDescription:
The property is well situated directly off of Highway 101, the north/south highway connecting the California, Oregon and Washington coastline (1,540 miles). The location is just west of the meeting point for Highway 101 and Highway 6. Highway 6 links Raymond to Chehalis approximately 51 miles to the east. Public beach access is just 10 miles to the west and this location serves a great last spot in or first spot out when traveling to the coast. The property sits on more than 4 acres, backs directly to the Willapa Bay and is served by nationally tenanted out parcels of McDonald’s and Shell Oil.

Raymond is a city in Pacific County, Washington along Willapa Bay. The town’s economy has traditionally been based on logging and fishing, together with a limited amount of tourism.

Willapa Bay is located on the southwest Pacific coast of Washington state. The Long Beach Peninsula separates Willapa Bay from the greater expanse of the Pacific Ocean. With over 120 square miles of surface area Willapa Bay is the second largest riverine estuary on the Pacific coast of the continental United States. Willapa Bay is known for its biodiversity and much of it, including the entirety of Long Island, has been set aside as part of the Willapa National Wildlife Refuge. The Willapa National Wildlife Refuge consists of over 17,000 acres of tidelands, temperate rainforests, ocean beaches, and small streams. It also includes several rare remnants of the old growth coastal cedar forest. Preserving habitat for spawning wild salmon, hundreds of thousands of migrating shorebirds and waterfowl, and threatened species such as the western snowy plover and marbled murrelet, the refuge is the place to see what the Pacific Northwest looked like over 100 years ago. The oyster beds help the ecosystem by providing habitats and filtering water, improving the quality of the water. The North River, Willapa River, and Naselle River provide most of the freshwater input into Willapa Bay. Other rivers that empty into Willapa Bay include the Bone River, Niawiakum River, Palix River, Cedar River and Bear River, among others.

Pacific County is centered on Willapa Bay, a region that provides twenty-five percent of the United States’ oyster harvest, although forestry, fishing, and tourism are also significant elements of the county’s economy. Pacific County‘s largest city is Raymond.

Riverside County, California is the fourth largest county in California and the tenth largest in the United States. It’s about 180 miles wide and covers more than 7,300 square miles. The county is home to 2.4 million residents. Riverside County was created in 1893 from parts of San Diego and San Bernardino counties. The county’s name comes from the City of Riverside, which was named in 1871 when the Santa Ana River’s upper canal reached it. Riverside is a city in and the county seat of Riverside County, which has 24 nationally registered historic sites and more than 100 city landmarks. It also offers a variety of museums, theaters, festivals, markets, and unique shopping experiences. Riverside the most populous city in the Inland Empire and in Riverside County, and is about 50 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles. Known for its citrus industry and as the city of arts and innovation, visitors and residents enjoy cultural activities including downtown museums, restaurants and performing arts centers. 



Riverside is also more affordable than major Golden State cities like Los Angeles or San Francisco. Due to Riverside’s warm, dry climate, the average electricity rates are 33% lower than the California average. The Riverside Chamber of Commerce says that the real estate market’s growth is Riverside’s main economic driver. Riverside’s transportation, retail, employment, innovation and private investment all make up an attractive environment for businesses. Riverside has experienced $1.5 billion in private investment in the past five years while Riverside County’s retail market has been resilient. In 2021, employment gains were largest in leisure services, professional business services, private education and healthcare, and retail trade.


The Inland Empire, which includes Riverside and San Bernardino Counties, has a network of innovation centers that drive investment and job growth. The City of Riverside is committed to building inclusive partnerships for sustainable, resilient economic development through strategies to stimulate a favorable investment climate, welcome entrepreneurship, encourage industry and talent diversity, expand living wage jobs and support our unique quality of place. As a world-class city of Arts and Innovation, Riverside is the city of choice in Southern California: a place where people of diverse talents choose to work and live and where entrepreneurs and businesses choose to locate and invest. The City offers a rich agricultural heritage, unique architecture, affordable housing stock and business friendly environment that is unique to Southern California.


Anchored by two historic performing arts centers managed by Live Nation, downtown Riverside offers the best in nightlife and entertainment, all within steps of the Riverside Convention Center and downtown hotels.  A lively restaurant, bar/pub and nightclub scene is a constant in downtown Riverside, with numerous annual festivals, including the famed six-week Festival of Lights (the Top Holiday Lighting event in the United States), the Lunar Fest, and Dicken’s Festival regularly enlivening downtown.

listings.description:
CBRE, as exclusive advisor, is pleased to present the opportunity to acquire 8247-8249 E 9th Street, a three-unit residential income property featuring a primary SFR and two newly constructed ADUs, located in the high-growth market of Rancho Cucamonga.

This well-located asset consists of a primary single-family residence originally built in 1953 and two newly constructed Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) completed in 2024. The property features a fully upgraded front home and two newly built modern ADUs. The architecture blends mid-century charm with contemporary construction, highlighted by new windows, doors, and a 28-panel solar system paired with a newly upgraded electrical service panel designed to significantly reduce energy costs. Interior features include hardwood-style laminate flooring, stainless steel appliances, and in-unit laundry for the new units. Residents enjoy comfortable living with wall-mounted AC and heating systems. The gated property offers enhanced security and features a two-car detached garage, along with on-site parking and ample street parking.

Financial Performance & Asset Value
The offering presents a rare multifamily investment in the Rancho Cucamonga market competitively priced at $1,200,000, or $400,000 per unit. The asset is marketed at $381 per square foot with a unit mix consisting of one 1-bedroom/1-bathroom unit and two 3-bedroom/2-bathroom units. This stable investment provides immediate income security with a current cap rate of 5.45%. Savvy investors can capitalize on a pro forma cap rate of 5.87%. The property features a combination of drought-resistant landscaping with artificial turf grass surrounded by mature trees for budget-friendly, low-maintenance operations.

Strategic Location & Regional Connectivity
Rancho Cucamonga is widely recognized as one of the most desirable places to live in San Bernardino County, consistently ranking among the top 3–5 cities in the region for lifestyle, safety, and amenities. The location highlights include prime positioning within the highly prestigious Chaffey Joint Union High School District, consistently ranked as the top district in the county. Residents benefit from being near Los Amigos Elementary School and major employment centers like San Antonio Regional Hospital and Chaffey College. Furthermore, the property is strategically located near the future Brightline West flagship station, which will connect Rancho Cucamonga to Las Vegas by 2029.

Whether for a first-time purchaser or a seasoned investor looking for a high-quality asset with minimal capital expenditure requirements, 8247-8249 E 9th Street offers an exceptional foothold in the thriving Inland Empire submarket.
listings.locationDescription:

Rancho Cucamonga stands as an economic powerhouse and is widely recognized as one of the most desirable places to live in San Bernardino County, consistently ranking among the top 3 to 5 cities in the region for overall quality of life. As the 4th most populated city in the county, it offers a sophisticated economic landscape characterized by high median household incomes—frequently ranking in the top 3—and a robust, diverse employment base. The city is an established hub for the medical and education sectors, anchored by major institutional drivers like San Antonio Regional Hospital and Chaffey College.

For an investor, the local market dynamics provide an ideal environment for long-term appreciation and low vacancy. The presence of the Etiwanda and Chaffey Joint Union High School Districts—ranked among the best in the county—acts as a permanent catalyst for housing demand, attracting an affluent and stable tenant base of families and working professionals. This high-quality demographic is further supported by strategic infrastructure investments, most notably the $12 billion Brightline West high-speed rail project. By transforming Rancho Cucamonga into a national transportation gateway, these developments ensure the city remains a premier destination for both residents and regional commerce, solidifying its status as a top-tier Inland Empire investment market.

Rancho Cucamonga offers some of Southern California’s finest retail and leisure destinations. Residents are minutes away from the 1.2 million-square-foot Victoria Gardens lifestyle center and the iconic Ontario Mills mall. Local entertainment is anchored by the Toyota Arena and the high-tech Topgolf complex. For outdoor enthusiasts, the Pacific Electric Trail provides miles of recreational paths, while the city’s overall ranking as a “Top Place to Live” ensures a vibrant local dining and social scene.

listings.headline: 13 Units in Prime Upland | 5.28% Cap Rate | 31% Rental Upside
listings.description:
CBRE is pleased to present the exclusive opportunity to acquire Subject Property, a premier 13-unit garden-style multifamily investment located in the high-demand core of Upland, California.

Offering a massive 31% rental upside, this well-maintained asset at 425 N 11th Avenue provides investors a rare combination of immediate cash flow and substantial long-term appreciation. Currently performing at a 5.28% CAP rate, the property offers a clear path to a 7.60% Pro Forma CAP rate upon stabilization. It is perfectly positioned within one of the Inland Empire’s most desirable and supply-constrained submarkets, known for its historic charm and strong residential roots.

Strategic Location & Connectivity
Known as the “City of Gracious Living,” Upland blends a quaint, small-town atmosphere with modern suburban convenience. Residents of 425 N 11th Avenue benefit from a sophisticated regional transportation network, enjoying seamless access to the I-10 and I-210 freeways, with the SR-57 and I-15 just minutes away. This central positioning serves as a vital commuter hub, connecting the workforce to major employment centers across San Bernardino, Los Angeles, Riverside, and Orange Counties, while the nearby Upland Metrolink Station provides effortless rail access.

The property is located just minutes from the vibrant Claremont Village and Upland’s historic downtown, featuring boutique dining, local cafes, and the cultural heart of the region. Furthermore, the asset is situated just minutes from the world-renowned San Antonio Regional Hospital, a premier 363-bed facility and major regional employer that serves as the area’s primary trauma center. Beyond local attractions, residents are a short drive from world-class retail destinations, including the Montclair Mall and Victoria Gardens, while the nearby Pacific Electric Bike Trail offers miles of outdoor recreation, ensuring a comprehensive “live-work-play” environment.

Exceptional Property & Unit Features
425 N 11th Avenue is defined by classic 1950s architecture and a professional blend of lush, mature landscaping that creates a serene residential atmosphere. Residents benefit from a functional amenity package that includes an on-site laundry facility and a mix of covered and surface parking, all within a well-manicured complex. The modernized interiors feature spacious layouts designed for contemporary living, highlighted by kitchens with updated fixtures and oven ranges and range hoods. These quality finishes are further enhanced by a combination of durable laminate wood plank flooring and carpeting, updated lighting, ceiling fans, and vertical blinds. Each residence ensures year-round comfort with dedicated wall-mounted A/C and heating units, while a premium front unit offers a private entrance, attached garage, and a walk-in closet for a truly residential feel.

Investment Stability & Opportunity
This stable, well-maintained asset provides immediate income security and remains a highly attractive destination for residents seeking quality housing in a premier submarket. The property’s proven performance and strategic location make it an ideal acquisition for a wide range of investors. Whether tailored for a first-time purchaser looking for a value-add project, a seasoned investor expanding a regional footprint, or a 1031 exchange buyer requiring a reliable, low-vacancy asset with significant upside, this offering provides long-term stability and an exceptional foothold in the thriving Inland Empire economy.
listings.locationDescription:
Covering 20,105 square miles, San Bernardino County is America’s largest county and a diverse public service organization governed by an elected Board of Supervisors and serving a community of nearly 2.2 million residents. San Bernardino County is comprised of more than 40 departments and agencies staffed by more than 25,000 public service professionals providing a wide range of vital services in areas that include public safety, health and human services, economic development, housing, recreation, and culture. San Bernardino County offers a variety of job opportunities in fields such as healthcare, public safety, and technology. Given San Bernardino County’s location and relative housing affordability in Southern California, it has become a substantial supplier of housing and construction-related jobs, which are a key employment sectors for the region. 


Upland, CA, located in the southern region of San Bernardino County, California, is a vibrant city nestled at the base of the majestic San Gabriel Mountains offering breathtaking scenery and opportunities for outdoor activities, just 35 miles east of Los Angeles. With a population of approximately 77,000 residents, Upland boasts a diverse demographic makeup, representing various ethnicities and age groups. Over the years, the city has seen sustained economic growth, particularly in the retail, healthcare, and education sectors. One of the key advantages of Upland is its central location in Southern California, making it an attractive destination for both residents and visitors. Positioned between major metropolitan areas like Los Angeles and San Bernardino, the city enjoys easy accessibility to essential transportation routes, including the 10 and 210 freeways. This strategic location enables seamless connections to neighboring cities and a plethora of attractions. The city is home to several shopping centers, hospitals, and schools, contributing to its overall economic growth and stability. Upland, CA offers a variety of shopping and entertainment options for residents and visitors alike. Beyond its convenient location, Upland offers an array of amenities and entertainment options. Upland is also in close proximity to renowned destinations such as Disneyland and Universal Studios, allowing for memorable day trips and family outings.


The Inland Empire, which includes Riverside and San Bernardino Counties, has a network of innovation centers that drive investment and job growth. San Bernardino County is committed to a thriving city possessing a sustainable system of high-quality education, community health, public safety, housing, retail, recreation, arts and culture and infrastructure. San Bernardino County envisions a world class region which capitalizes on its location, the diversity of its people and its economy to create a broad range of choices for its residents in how they live, work, and play. In addition, it strives for a continual vibrant economy with a skilled workforce that attracts employers who seek the unique opportunities the region has to offer and provide jobs that create area-wide prosperity. 


Upland, CA, is home to a robust healthcare infrastructure designed to meet the diverse medical needs of the region. At the forefront of this exceptional landscape is the renowned San Antonio Regional Hospital, a leading 363-bed facility widely recognized for its commitment to clinical excellence. As one of the area’s primary trauma centers, the hospital provides critical emergency services along with comprehensive care in advanced surgery and specialized treatments for oncology, cardiology, and orthopedics. Supplemented by a multitude of local clinics and private practices, Upland offers residents world-class medical security within minutes of their front door.

listings.locationDescription:
Salem–Willamette Valley Airport (IATA: SLE), is a public-use airport located 
approximately two miles southeast of downtown Salem, Oregon, serving 
Oregon’s capital city and the broader Willamette Valley region. Owned and 
operated by the City of Salem, the airport covers roughly 750 acres and supports 
a diverse mix of general aviation, business aviation, flight training, and Oregon 
Army National Guard operations. After several years without scheduled service, 
limited commercial passenger flights returned in 2023, reconnecting Salem 
to select destinations in the western United States and improving regional 
accessibility. SLE plays an important regional role by supporting emergency 
response, military readiness, and economic development. Recent investments 
in infrastructure and terminal planning are aimed at strengthening resiliency and 
positioning the airport for future growth. Commercial air service at the airport 
has generated an estimated $19 million in economic impact for the local area in 
its first year, underscoring the airport’s importance to the Salem-area economy 
and the Willamette Valley as a whole

restaurants, movie theaters, grocery stores, bakeries, coffee shops, clothing stores
and banking institutions along Route 66 and major thoroughfares linking to East and

listings.locationDescription:
Often called the “Canyon City,” Azusa is a charming and vibrant community nestled at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains, about 25 miles northeast of Los Angeles.

Known for its scenic beauty, outdoor recreation, and rich history, Azusa offers the perfect blend of small-town charm and modern convenience.

The city is famous for its access to the beautiful San Gabriel River Trail and the Angeles National Forest, making it a paradise for hikers, bikers, and nature enthusiasts. Home to Azusa Pacific University, the city also boasts a youthful, welcoming atmosphere with a strong sense of community.

Whether exploring historic Route 66, enjoying local eateries, or taking in mountain views, Azusa is a hidden gem with a lot to offer.
